title: Microbatch Thermostat: sequence-length sentinel & aggressive pad reclamation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: reduce wasted padding and improve throughput/cost without regressing tail latency by introducing a lightweight 'microbatch thermostat' that observes incoming request seqlen distributions and adjusts bucket boundaries, prefill placement, and kernel hints in real time.

Background: Current bucketing is static per-minute histograms and applies conservative pad budgets, which leaves 8-20% of token compute wasted in our benchmarks for mixed short+long traffic. We need a runtime component that can: 1) detect rapid shifts in observed sequence-length modes, 2) shrink/expand microbatch bucket cut points with safety hysteresis, and 3) opportunistically reclaim padding during prefill when decoder/encoder state allows.

Design summary:
- Sequence-length sentinel: lightweight streaming estimator that keeps an exponentially-weighted histogram of recent request lengths (prefill and decode). Emits candidate boundary shifts when the 95th/50th percentiles change beyond configurable thresholds (default: 12% relative).
- Thermostat controller: uses a PID-like control loop with two knobs: aggressiveness (how fast boundaries move) and safety-margin (minimum advantage required to change). The thermostat outputs target bucket cuts and an integer pad-budget per bucket.
- Pad reclamation in prefill: prefill scheduler probes in-batch KV cache reuse and per-request effective length. For requests that have large trailing pads but short effective context (e.g., trimmed prompts or system messages), reclaim trailing pad tokens and mark those microbatches as 'packed' for kernel selection to prefer reduced-row kernels.
- Kernel & attention hints: Runtime emits kernel selection hints per microbatch: compact-row vs padded-row, and attention-mode suggestion (full vs windowed vs sparse projection) based on observed max seqlen and hardware occupancy. These are advisory; final kernel decision still takes place in the kernel selector but uses hints to bias cost model.
- Prefill/decode scheduling interplay: Prefill prioritization is adjusted so that when thermostat signals large pad savings in short-request buckets, prefill throughput is increased (larger microbatch sizes for short buckets) while decode lane weight is preserved for interactive SLOs. We maintain token latency SLOs by reserving minimal decode slots and only applying aggressive packing when tail latency has headroom.

Success metrics:
- 8-18% reduction in padded tokens served across mixed workloads in staging benchmark suite (conservative goal: 8% overall; optimistic: 18% for highly bimodal traffic).
- No more than 5% regression in 99th-percentile per-token latency for interactive decode under baseline loads.
- Cost-per-1M-token reduction measurable in daily billing dashboard for affected customers.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrumentation (2): add lightweight EWMA histogram & telemetry counters; add kernel-hint field to microbatch descriptor.
2) Thermostat prototype (3): implement controller in runtime as a separate actor with config flags for aggressiveness and hysteresis.
3) Prefill reclaim hook (3): detect trailing-pad candidates and expose an opt-in reclaim path guarded by feature flag.
4) Kernel hint integration (2): plumb hint into kernel selector and fall back to current path if mismatch.
5) Integration tests & microbench (3): create synthetic mixed-length traffic tests, measure pad tokens, throughput, and latency.
6) Canary rollout (1): start with a small subset of hosts, monitor SLOs and pad metrics, then widen.

Rollout & safety: default thermostat aggressiveness=low; full rollout only after two consecutive 48hr canary passes. On any >5% 99p latency regression, thermostat switches to conservative mode and a rollback job triggers.

Notes: This intentionally separates the 'thermostat' decisioning from the kernel selector so we can A/B thermostat policies without touching kernel selector logic. The thermostat produces deterministic, auditable events that will be logged to observability for postmortem analysis.

2025-02-20 - Diego Martinez: Added prefilling reclaim prototype. Edge case: requests with appended user-provided whitespace caused incorrect reclaim; added canonicalizer to trim client-side trailing whitespace before reclaiming.
